title: 08. GraphRAG: Graph Query Languages
summary: Graph databases use specialised query languages designed for traversing relationships efficiently. Cypher (Neo4j) uses a declarative, ASCII-art pattern syntax ((n)-[:REL]->(m)) that is highly readable and optimised for property graphs.

sections.title: ① Concept Explanation
sections.body: Graph databases use specialised query languages designed for traversing relationships efficiently. **Cypher** (Neo4j) uses a declarative, ASCII-art pattern syntax (`(n)-[:REL]->(m)`) that is highly readable and optimised for property graphs. **SPARQL** (W3C standard, used by RDF stores like Amazon Neptune, Wikidata) uses triple patterns and is the standard for semantic web and ontology queries. **Gremlin** (Apache TinkerPop, used by Amazon Neptune, JanusGraph, CosmosDB) is a functional, traversal-oriented language using method chaining — more explicit but flexible for complex path queries. **Text-to-Cypher/SPARQL** uses LLMs to translate natural language to graph queries, enabling Graph RAG to dynamically generate precise graph queries from user questions rather than relying on fixed traversal patterns. A critical production concern: **query injection prevention** — LLM-generated queries must be validated and parameterised before execution.

sections.title: ④ Visual Explanation
sections.body:
```
         GRAPH QUERY LANGUAGES IN GRAPH RAG PIPELINE

  NATURAL LANGUAGE QUERY
  "What companies did Sequoia Capital invest in during 2023?"
                │
                ▼
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │         TEXT-TO-CYPHER (LLM)            │
  │                                         │
  │  Prompt: Schema + few-shot examples     │
  │                                         │
  │  Generated:                             │
  │  MATCH (vc:Entity {name: $vc_name})     │
  │    -[r:INVESTED_IN]->(co:Entity)        │
  │  WHERE r.year = $year                   │
  │  RETURN co.name, r.amount               │
  │  LIMIT 50                               │
  └──────────────┬──────────────────────────┘
                 │
                 ▼
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │         VALIDATION LAYER                │
  │                                         │
  │  ✓ No DETACH DELETE                     │
  │  ✓ No CALL dbms.*                       │
  │  ✓ Has LIMIT clause                     │
  │  ✓ Relation type in allowlist           │
  │  ✓ Parameters used (not f-strings)      │
  │                                         │
  │  BLOCK if any check fails               │
  └──────────────┬──────────────────────────┘
                 │
                 ▼
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │         GRAPH DATABASE                  │
  │                                         │
  │  Neo4j    → Cypher                      │
  │  Neptune  → Gremlin or SPARQL           │
  │  ArangoDB → AQL                         │
  │  Cosmos   → Gremlin                     │
  └──────────────┬──────────────────────────┘
                 │
                 ▼
  QUERY RESULT → LLM ANSWER GENERATION

  LANGUAGE COMPARISON
  ┌─────────────┬──────────────────────┬────────────────────┐
  │ Language    │ Pattern              │ DB                 │
  ├─────────────┼──────────────────────┼────────────────────┤
  │ Cypher      │ (n)-[:R]->(m)        │ Neo4j, Memgraph    │
  │ SPARQL      │ ?s :rel ?o           │ Neptune RDF        │
  │ Gremlin     │ g.V().out().values() │ Neptune, JanusGraph│
  │ AQL         │ FOR v IN GRAPH       │ ArangoDB           │
  └─────────────┴──────────────────────┴────────────────────┘

  CYPHER INJECTION ATTACK EXAMPLE
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  User input: " ' OR 1=1 MATCH (n) DETACH DELETE n //"   │
  │                                                          │
  │  UNSAFE query:                                           │
  │  MATCH (e {name: '' OR 1=1 MATCH (n) DETACH DELETE n})  │
  │  → DELETES ALL NODES                                     │
  │                                                          │
  │  SAFE: Use parameters                                    │
  │  MATCH (e {name: $name}) WHERE $name = <user input>      │
  │  → Neo4j escapes input automatically                     │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
